questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Consider the function $y = f(x)$ defined implicitly by the equation $y^3 - 3y + x = 0$ on the interval $(-\infty, -2) \cup (2, \infty)$. The area of the region bounded by the curve $y = f(x)$, the x-axis and the lines $x = a, x = b$, where $-\infty < a < b < -2$ is
questions.solution:
Given the implicit equation $y^3 - 3y + x = 0$, we can write $x = 3y - y^3$.

For $x \in (-\infty, -2)$, we have $3y - y^3 < -2$, which implies $y^3 - 3y - 2 > 0$. Factoring this gives $(y+1)^2(y-2) > 0$, which means $y > 2$.

Since $y = f(x) > 2$ for all $x \in (-\infty, -2)$, the function $f(x)$ is strictly positive in the interval $[a, b]$. Thus, the area of the bounded region is given by:

$A = \displaystyle\int_a^{b} f(x) \, dx$

Using integration by parts, taking $u = f(x)$ and $dv = dx$:

$A = [x f(x)]_a^{b} - \displaystyle\int_a^{b} x f'(x) \, dx$

$A = b f(b) - a f(a) - \displaystyle\int_a^{b} x f'(x) \, dx$

To find $f'(x)$, we differentiate the given equation $y^3 - 3y + x = 0$ with respect to $x$:

$3y^2 \dfrac{dy}{dx} - 3 \dfrac{dy}{dx} + 1 = 0$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} (3y^2 - 3) = -1$

$f'(x) = \dfrac{-1}{3(y^2 - 1)} = \dfrac{-1}{3((f(x))^2 - 1)}$

Substituting $f'(x)$ back into the area expression:

$A = b f(b) - a f(a) - \displaystyle\int_a^{b} x \left( \dfrac{-1}{3((f(x))^2 - 1)} \right) \, dx$

$A = \displaystyle\int_a^{b} \dfrac{x \, dx}{3((f(x))^2 - 1)} + b f(b) - a f(a)$

Answer: $\displaystyle\int_a^{b} \dfrac{x\,dx}{3((f(x))^2 - 1)} + bf(b) - af(a)$

questions.solution: We have, $y=x+1 \text{$ and $} y=\cos x \begin{aligned} \text{ Require area } &=\int_{-1}^{0}(x+1) d x+\int_{0}^{\pi / 2} \cos x d x \\ &=\left[\frac{x^{2}}{2}+x\right]_{-1}^{0}+[\sin x]_{0}^{\pi / 2} \\ &=\left[(0)-\left(\frac{1}{2}-1\right)\right]+[1-0] \\ &=\frac{1}{2}+1=\frac{3}{2} \text{ sq unit. } \end{aligned}$

questions.q: The area of the region lying above $X$ -axis, and included between the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}=2 a x$ and the parabola $y^{2}=a x, a > 0$ is
questions.solution: Given, equation of circle $x^{2}+y^{2}=2 a x\Rightarrow(x-a)^{2}+y^{2}=a^{2}$ and equation of parabola is $y^{2}=a x, a > 0$ Intersection points of circle and parabola $\begin{array}{lr}\Rightarrow & x^{2}+a x=2 a x \\ \Rightarrow & x^{2}=a x\end{array}\Rightarrow \quad x^{2}-a x=0\Rightarrow \quad x(x-a)=0\Rightarrow \quad x=0, a$ Intersecting points are $(0,0)$ and $(a, a)\therefore$ Required area $=\frac{\pi a^{2}}{4}-\int_{0}^{a} \sqrt{a x}d x=\frac{\pi a^{2}}{4}-\sqrt{a}\left(\frac{x^{3 / 2}}{3 / 2}\right)_{0}^{a}=\frac{\pi a^{2}}{4}-\frac{2 a^{2}}{3}= a^{2} \left(\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac{2}{3}\right)$

questions.q: The area of the figure bounded by the parabolas $x=-2 y^{2}$ and $x=1-3 y^{2}$ is
questions.solution: We have, $x=-2 y^{2} \Rightarrow \quad y^{2}=-\frac{1}{2} x$ ...(i) and $\quad x=1-3 y^{2} \Rightarrow y^{2}=-\frac{1}{3}(x-1)$ ...(ii) From Eqs. (i) and (ii),we get. $\begin{aligned} &-\frac{1}{2} x=-\frac{1}{3}(x-1) \\ \Rightarrow & 3 x=2(x-1) \\ \Rightarrow & 3 x=2 x-2 \\ \Rightarrow & x=-2 \\ \Rightarrow & y^{2}=-\frac{1}{2}(-2)=1 \\ \Rightarrow & y=\pm 1 \end{aligned} \therefore$ Point of intersection of two curves is $(-2 \pm 1)$ $\therefore$ Required Area $=2 \int_{0}^{1} \sin x d x =2\left[y-\frac{y^{3}}{3}\right]_{0}^{1}$ =2$\left[1-\frac{1}{3}\right]$ =$\frac{4}{3} \mathrm{sq}$ units

(i) and (ii),we get. $\begin{aligned} &-\frac{1}{2} x=-\frac{1}{3}(x-1) \\ \Rightarrow & 3 x=2(x-1) \\ \Rightarrow & 3 x=2 x-2 \\ \Rightarrow & x=-2 \\ \Rightarrow & y^{2}=-\frac{1}{2}(-2)=1 \\ \Rightarrow & y=\pm 1 \end{aligned} \therefore$ Point of intersection of two curves is $(-2 \pm 1)$ $\therefore$ Required Area $=2 \int_{0}^{1} \sin x d x =2\left[y-\frac{y^{3}}{3}\right]_{0}^{1}$ =2$\left[1-\frac{1}{3}\right]$ =$\frac{4}{3} \mathrm{sq}$ units

Then \begin{aligned} A &=\int_{-1}^{1}\left(\sqrt{5-x^{2}}+ x-1\right) d x+\int_{1}^{2}\left(\sqrt{5-x^{2}}- x+1\right) d x \\ &=\int_{-1}^{1} \sqrt{5-x^{2}} d x+\int_{1}^{2} \sqrt{5-x^{2}} d x +\int_{-1}^{1}(x-1) d x+\int_{1}^{2}(-x+1) d x \\ &=\int_{-1}^{2} \sqrt{5-x^{2}} d x+\left[\frac{x^{2}}{2}- x\right]^{1}_{-1}+\left[-\frac{x^{2}}{2}+ x\right]_{1}^{2} \\ &=\left[\frac{1}{2} x \sqrt{5-x^{2}}+\frac{5}{2} \sin ^{-1} \frac{x}{\sqrt{5}}\right]_{-1}^{2}-\frac{5}{2}\\ &=1+\frac{5}{2} \sin ^{-1} \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}+1+\frac{5}{2} \sin ^{-1} \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}-\frac{5}{2}\\ &=-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{5}{2} \sin ^{-1} \left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \times \sqrt{1-\frac{1}{5}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \sqrt{1-\frac{4}{5}}\right)\\ &=-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{5}{2} \sin ^^^{-1}(1)=\frac{5 \pi}{4}-\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{squnits} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: The area of the region bounded by the curve $y=x^3$ its tangent at (1,1) and X-axis is
questions.solution: We have, $y=x^{3}$ and $A(1,1)\therefore\frac{d y}{d x}=3 x^{2}$ On putting $x=1$ in $\mathrm{Eq}$. $\frac{d y}{d x}=3(1)^{2}=3\therefore$ Equation of tangent at $A(1,1)$ is $y-1=3(x-1) \Rightarrow y=3 x-2$ $\therefore$ Required area $=\int_{0}^{1} x^{3} d x-\int_{2 / 3}^{1}(3 x-2) d x=\left[\frac{x^{4}}{4}\right]_{0}^{1}-\left[\frac{3 x^{2}}{2}-2 x\right]_{2 / 3}^{1}=\frac{1}{4}-\left[\left(\frac{3}{2}-2\right)-\left(\frac{2}{3}-\frac{4}{3}\right)\right]=\frac{1}{12} \mathrm{sq}$ unit

questions.q: The area of the region bounded by the curves $y=x^{2}$ and $x=y^{2}$ is
questions.solution: Given curves are $y=x^{2}$ and $x=y^{2}$, which is the form of parabola. The point of intersection, $x=\left(x^{2}\right)^{2} \begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow \quad x=x^{4} \Rightarrow x\left(1-x^{3}\right)=0 \\ \Rightarrow \quad x=0 \text{ and } 1=x^{3} \\ \Rightarrow \quad x=0 \text{ and } x=1 \\ \text{ When } x=0, \text{ then } y=0 \\ \text{ When } x=1, \text{ then } y=1^{2}=1 \end{array} \therefore$ The point of intersection is (0,0) and (1,1) $\therefore$ Area of shaded region $\begin{array}{l} =\int_{0}^{1}$$\left($y_{2}-y_{1}\right) d x \\ =\int_{0}^{1}$\left[\sqrt{x}-$x^{2}\right] d x=$\left[\frac{x^{3 / 2}}{3 / 2}-\frac{x^{3}}{3}\right]_{0}^{1}$\\ =$\frac{2}{3}($1)^{3 / 2}-$\frac{(1)^{3}}{3}-$0-0 \\ =$\frac{2}{3}-\frac{1}{3}=\frac{1}{3} \mathrm{sq} \text{ units } \end{array}$

questions.solution: Given equation of parabola is y=x^{2}-4 x+5 $\Rightarrow \quad y=(x-2)^{2}+1\Rightarrow \quad(x-2)^{2}=(y-1)$ and equation of line is $\begin{array}{r} y=x+1 \\ \Rightarrow \quad x-y=-1 \end{array} $$ On putting the value of $(y-1)$ from Eqs. (ii) in (1). we get (x-2)^{2}=x \Rightarrow x^{2}+4-4 x=x \Rightarrow \quad x^{2}-5 x+4=0\Rightarrow x^{2}-4 x-x+4=0\Rightarrow \quad x(x-4)-1(x-4)=0\Rightarrow \quad(x-1)(x-4)=0$ or $x=1,4$ then from is (ii) $y=2,5\therefore$ Required area $=\int_{1}^{4}\left\{(x+1)-\left(x^{2}-4 x+5\right)\right\} d x=\int_{1}^{4}\left(-x^{2}+5 x-4\right) d x=\left[\frac{-x^{3}}{3}+\frac{5 x^{2}}{2}-4 x\right]_{1}^{4}=\left[-\frac{64}{3}+40-16+\frac{1}{3}-\frac{5}{2}+4\right]=\left(-21-\frac{3}{2}+28\right)=\frac{9}{2}$

questions.q: If $f(x)=x^{2 / 3}, x \geq 0.$ Then, the area of the region enclosed by the curve $y=f(x)$ and the three lines $y=x, x=1$ and $x=8$ is
questions.solution: Given, $f(x)=x^{2 / 3}, x \geq 0$ and line $y=x$ $\therefore$ Required area $A=\int_{x=1}^{8}\left(x-x^{2 / 3}\right) d x=\left[\frac{x^{2}}{2}-\frac{3}{5} x^{5 / 3}\right]_{1}^{9}=\left(32-\frac{3}{5} \times 32\right)-\left(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{3}{5}\right)=32 \times \frac{2}{5}-\frac{(5-6)}{10}=\frac{64}{5}+\frac{1}{10}=\frac{128+1}{10}=\frac{129}{10}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area of the region enclosed between parabola $y^{2}=x$ and the line $y=m x$ is $\frac{1}{48}$ Then, the value of $m$ is
questions.solution: Equation of parabola is $y^{2}=x$ and line $y=m x$ For intersection point of both curves put $x=y^{2}$, we get y=m y^{2} \Rightarrow y(m y-1)=0 $\Rightarrow \quad y=0$ or $y=\frac{1}{m}$ Then, $\quad x=0$ or $x=\frac{1}{m^{2}}\therefore$ Intersection points are (0,0) and $P\left(\frac{1}{m^{2}}, \frac{1}{m}\right)\therefore$ Required area $=\int_{0}^{1 / m}\left(\frac{y}{m}-y^{2}\right)|d y=|\left[\frac{y^{2}}{2 m}-\frac{y^{3}}{3}\right]_{0}^{1 / m} \mid=\left|\frac{1}{2 m^{3}}-\frac{1}{3 m^{3}}\right|=\left|\frac{1}{6 m^{3}}\right|=\frac{1}{48}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{6 m^{3}}=\pm \frac{1}{48} \Rightarrow m^{3}=\pm 8$ (given) Now, if $m^{3}=8\Rightarrow \quad m^{3}=(2)^{3} \Rightarrow m=2$ If $\quad m^{3}=-8\Rightarrow \quad m^{3}=(-2)^{3} \Rightarrow m=-2$
